state_overtime_notes: Daily and weekly overtime does not apply to employers of fewer than 4 employees. An approved flexible plan can set a 10-hour day.

double_time_rule: After 12 hr/day; >8 hr on 7th consecutive day
state_overtime_notes: Double time after 12 hours in a day. On the 7th day of work in a workweek: first 8 hours at 1.5x, over 8 at 2x.
Daily overtime after 12 hours in a workday or 12 consecutive hours.
Restaurants and hotel restaurants pay 1.5x the minimum rate on the 7th consecutive day.
Employees guaranteed $4,000 or more a month are exempt from state minimum wage and overtime law.
Employees who work all 7 days of a workweek get 1.5x for hours on the 7th day. This does not apply when the employee may not work over 40 hours in the week.
State law premium starts after 48 hours. FLSA-covered employees still get overtime after 40.
Seasonal amusement or recreation businesses pay premium after 52 hours.
Daily overtime after 8 hours applies only to employees earning less than 1.5x the state minimum wage ($18.00 an hour).
Live-in residential workers get premium pay after 44 hours.
Seasonal amusement or recreation establishments pay premium after 45 hours.
Premium after 10 hours a day in canneries, driers, packing plants, mills, factories and manufacturing (some mills excluded).
Retail and certain other businesses pay 1.5x for Sunday and holiday work.
Premium pay does not apply to employees who request comp time instead.
